business_problem: MPL needed real-time visibility across gameplay, app, and transaction events because batch-driven systems delayed fraud detection, personalization, and product decisions for a 90-million-user gaming platform.
solution_summary: MPL built its new trust and personalization backbone on a fully managed Kafka solution from Confluent so gameplay, app, and competition events could move continuously instead of arriving a day late from batch systems. Kafka carries streams from gameplay activity, player actions, and competition outcomes into a real-time pipeline that feeds authorization services and downstream data science workflows. That architecture lets MPL identify suspicious behavior quickly enough to block, lock, or suspend users before fraud and money-laundering issues spread, while the same event streams power tailored onboarding, retention offers, and in-product tasks based on gaming behavior. Because Confluent manages the Kafka deployment, MPL can support its multicloud transition and growing pipeline count without hiring extra specialists to operate clusters. The result is a single streaming foundation for security, personalization, and product decisioning across the gaming platform.

business_outcome: MPL improved fraud prevention and platform trust, gave teams fresher signals for onboarding and retention offers, avoided adding Kafka operations headcount, and created a more scalable real-time foundation for new features.
